accepted.s: In the Gade Sai Krishna custodial-death case, the NHRC directed which combination of authorities to submit a report?
o: The Union Home Ministry, DGP and District Collector
The State Election Commission, DGP and Chief Justice of the High Court
The Governor, Speaker and Advocate-General of Andhra Pradesh
The Andhra Pradesh SHRC, DGP and Chief Secretary
accepted.x: In the Gade Sai Krishna case, the NHRC directed the Andhra Pradesh SHRC, the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary to report.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-and-function trap by distinguishing reporting authorities from constitutional offices.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission - establishment, seat after bifurcation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reports of Human Rights Commissions:
1. The annual report of the NHRC is sent to the Central Government and the concerned State Government.
2. The annual report of the NHRC is laid before each House of Parliament along with a memorandum of action taken.
3. Reports of a State Human Rights Commission are laid before the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The NHRC report is sent to the appropriate governments and laid before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum, while an SHRC report is laid before the State Legislature.
accepted.tq: Separate the report-sending authority from the legislature before which the report is laid.
accepted.sec: NHRC annual report → laid before; GANHRI accreditation

accepted.s: The annual report of the National Human Rights Commission is laid before Parliament together with which of the following?
o: A report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
The annual financial statement of the Commission
A statement of judicial review by the Supreme Court
A memorandum of action taken
accepted.x: The NHRC annual report is laid before each House of Parliament along with a memorandum of action taken.
accepted.tq: Test the precise accompanying document instead of the broad destination of the report.
accepted.sec: NHRC annual report → laid before; GANHRI accreditation

accepted.s: Accreditation of a National Human Rights Institution by GANHRI primarily depends on its conformity with which principles?
o: The Geneva Conventions
The Basic Structure doctrine
The Directive Principles of State Policy
The Paris Principles
accepted.x: GANHRI accreditation depends on conformity with the Paris Principles, which concern independence and effectiveness of national human-rights institutions.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between international standards governing institutions and other legal instruments.
accepted.sec: NHRC annual report → laid before; GANHRI accreditation

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Paris Principles?
o: They prescribe the procedure for prosecuting custodial deaths before Human Rights Courts.
They prescribe standards of independence, pluralism and a broad mandate for national human-rights institutions.
They establish the jurisdiction of State Human Rights Commissions over Union Territories.
They classify national human-rights institutions as A or B categories.
accepted.x: The Paris Principles, adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993, set standards of independence, pluralism and a broad mandate for national human-rights institutions.
accepted.tq: Match the international principles with their institutional purpose, not with accreditation labels or domestic jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: NHRC annual report → laid before; GANHRI accreditation

accepted.s: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 was framed in the light of which of the following?
o: The ICCPR and ICESCR adopted in 1976
The PUCL guidelines on encounter deaths issued in 2014
Paris Principles adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993
GANHRI accreditation rules adopted in 2019
accepted.x: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 was framed in the light of the Paris Principles, which were adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993.
accepted.tq: Use the year-and-instrument distinction to avoid confusing the Paris Principles with covenants or later guidelines.
accepted.sec: NHRC annual report → laid before; GANHRI accreditation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about GANHRI accreditation:
1. GANHRI accredits national human-rights institutions.
2. The categories include ‘A’ for fully compliant institutions and ‘B’ for other institutions.
3. Accreditation is unrelated to institutional independence and effectiveness.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Accreditation is connected with conformity to the Paris Principles, including independence and effectiveness, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the relationship between accreditation and institutional independence.
accepted.sec: NHRC annual report → laid before; GANHRI accreditation

accepted.s: The Supreme Court entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the implementation of which law in 1997?
o: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
accepted.x: In 1997, the Supreme Court entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976.
accepted.tq: Pair the judicial direction with the exact statute rather than a neighbouring social-justice law.
accepted.sec: Specialised NHRC mandates - bonded labour, custodial deaths, encounter deaths

accepted.s: In cases of custodial death, information is required to be reported to the NHRC within what period?
o: Seven days
48 hours
24 hours
12 hours
accepted.x: Custodial deaths are to be reported to the NHRC within 24 hours; post-mortem videography and independent investigation are also associated safeguards.
accepted.tq: Test the exact reporting deadline using nearby but distinct time intervals as distractors.
accepted.sec: Specialised NHRC mandates - bonded labour, custodial deaths, encounter deaths

accepted.s:
Which of the following safeguards are associated with NHRC handling of custodial deaths?
1. Reporting to the NHRC within 24 hours
2. Videography of the post-mortem examination
3. Independent investigation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three are specified safeguards associated with custodial-death cases: prompt reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.
accepted.tq: Group related procedural safeguards while checking whether the time requirement is included.
accepted.sec: Specialised NHRC mandates - bonded labour, custodial deaths, encounter deaths

accepted.s: Encounter deaths are associated with which of the following requirements under NHRC guidelines and PUCL v. Maharashtra (2014)?
o: Reporting and magisterial inquiry
Prior approval of the State Legislature
Only a departmental inquiry by the police
Automatic trial before the NHRC
accepted.x: NHRC guidelines and PUCL v. Maharashtra (2014) require reporting and a magisterial inquiry in cases of encounter deaths.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a required inquiry from an incorrect claim of automatic trial or legislative approval.
accepted.sec: Specialised NHRC mandates - bonded labour, custodial deaths, encounter deaths

accepted.s: Which of the following was included in the NHRC’s Advisory 2.0 on transgender welfare issued in May 2026?
o: Transfer of all transgender cases to Human Rights Courts
Abolition of all State Human Rights Commissions
Census categories, legal-aid cells and expansion of Garima Greh
A single national category in place of all census classifications
accepted.x: The May 2026 Advisory 2.0 addressed census categories, legal-aid cells and expansion of Garima Greh.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise components of a specialised advisory and reject institutional or jurisdictional substitutions.
accepted.sec: Specialised NHRC mandates - bonded labour, custodial deaths, encounter deaths

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Institutional position)
a. National Commission for Minorities
b. National Commission for Backward Classes
c. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
d. Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities

List-II (Status as deemed member of NHRC)
i. Added in 2019
 ii. Deemed member before 2019

Select the correct code.
o: a–ii, b–i, c–i, d–i
a–i, b–ii, c–ii, d–i
a–ii, b–ii, c–i, d–i
a–i, b–i, c–ii, d–ii
accepted.x: The National Commission for Minorities was a deemed member before 2019. The National Commission for Backward Classes, National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities were added in 2019.
accepted.tq: Start with the older commission and then place the three 2019 additions together.
accepted.sec: Deemed members - chairpersons of other national commissions  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Before the additions made in 2019, which group consisted of deemed members of the NHRC?
o: National Commissions for Minorities, Backward Classes and Child Rights
Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities and National Commissions for SCs and STs
National Commissions for Backward Classes, Child Rights and Persons with Disabilities
National Commissions for Minorities, SCs, STs and Women
accepted.x: Before 2019, the chairpersons of the National Commissions for Minorities, SCs, STs and Women were included as deemed members of the NHRC.
accepted.tq: Use the before-and-after membership distinction to avoid mixing the 2019 additions with the earlier group.
accepted.sec: Deemed members - chairpersons of other national commissions  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities functions under which provision?
o: Section 2(28) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Section 75(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code
accepted.x: The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities functions under Section 75(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
accepted.tq: Apply the section-and-statute pairing method rather than confusing a disability provision with a human-rights provision.
accepted.sec: Deemed members - chairpersons of other national commissions  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is included in the statutory meaning of ‘human rights’ under the Protection of Human Rights Act?
o: Rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity enforceable by courts in India
Only rights expressly listed in the Fundamental Duties
Rights available exclusively to citizens during a national emergency
All customary rights irrespective of their enforceability in India
accepted.x: Human rights are rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants and enforceable by courts in India.
accepted.tq: Look for the complete definition, including both the subject matter and enforceability requirement.
accepted.sec: Act definitions - human rights, public servant status  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
The International Covenants referred to in the statutory understanding of human rights are the:
1. International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
2. International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
3. International Covenant on Environmental Protection
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 only
2 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The relevant International Covenants are the ICCPR and the ICESCR, both adopted in 1966. There is no third covenant named the International Covenant on Environmental Protection in this context.
accepted.tq: Reject the look-alike third item by identifying the two exact covenant names.
accepted.sec: Act definitions - human rights, public servant status  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: For the purpose of the Protection of Human Rights Act, the Chairperson, members and officers of the Commission are deemed to be:
o: Judicial officers only
Civil servants of the Union Government
Public servants
Members of Parliament
accepted.x: The Chairperson, members and officers of the Commission are deemed to be public servants under the relevant legal provision.
accepted.tq: Distinguish statutory deemed status from actual appointment to a government service.
accepted.sec: Act definitions - human rights, public servant status  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statutory reference reflects the change in the provision concerning the deemed public-servant status of Commission personnel?
o: Section 21 of the IPC, now Section 2(28) of the BNS from 1 July 2024
Section 21 of the PHRA, now Section 2(28) of the Constitution
Section 2(28) of the IPC, now Section 21 of the BNS from 1 July 2024
Section 75(1) of the RPwD Act, now Section 21 of the BNS
accepted.x: The earlier reference was Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code; from 1 July 2024, the corresponding reference is Section 2(28) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
accepted.tq: Separate the old and new statute numbers before matching the date of transition.
accepted.sec: Act definitions - human rights, public servant status  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the jurisdiction of State Human Rights Commissions:
1. An SHRC inquires into violations relating to subjects in the State List.
2. An SHRC inquires into violations relating to subjects in the Concurrent List.
3. An SHRC has jurisdiction over every subject, whereas the NHRC is restricted to the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: An SHRC deals with subjects in the State List and Concurrent List. The third statement reverses the respective jurisdictions; the NHRC covers all subjects.
accepted.tq: Catch the reversed comparison between the broad jurisdiction of the NHRC and the limited jurisdiction of an SHRC.
accepted.sec: Division of functions between NHRC and SHRCs - jurisdiction, UTs  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position regarding Union Territories after the 2019 change?
o: Every Union Territory must constitute an independent SHRC, including Delhi.
The Central Government may confer the human-rights functions of a Union Territory on an SHRC, while Delhi’s functions are handled by the NHRC.
Only the concerned State Government may confer Union Territory functions on an SHRC.
The NHRC has no role in the human-rights functions of Union Territories.
accepted.x: The Central Government may confer the human-rights functions of a Union Territory on an SHRC. Delhi’s human-rights functions are handled by the NHRC itself.
accepted.tq: Ask who holds the power and then distinguish Delhi’s special position from the general rule.
accepted.sec: Division of functions between NHRC and SHRCs - jurisdiction, UTs  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about constituting a State Human Rights Commission is correct?
o: An SHRC can be constituted only by Parliament through a constitutional amendment.
A State Government may constitute an SHRC under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
Every State Government is constitutionally required to constitute an SHRC.
Only the NHRC can constitute an SHRC.
accepted.x: Constitution of an SHRC is optional; the State Government may constitute one under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
accepted.tq: Test the significance of the word ‘may’ by contrasting an optional power with a mandatory duty.
accepted.sec: Division of functions between NHRC and SHRCs - jurisdiction, UTs  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: For speedy trial of offences arising from human-rights violations, a Human Rights Court is notified in each district by the State Government with the concurrence of:
o: The Governor alone
The Chairperson of the NHRC
The Chief Justice of the High Court
The Union Home Minister
accepted.x: The State Government notifies a Court of Session in each district as a Human Rights Court with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the required judicial concurrence.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Courts - district designation, Special Public Prosecutor  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A Human Rights Court designated for a district is ordinarily which type of court?
o: Court of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class
Executive Magistrate’s Court
Court of Session
High Court Bench
accepted.x: The State Government notifies a Court of Session in each district as a Human Rights Court for speedy trial of offences arising from human-rights violations.
accepted.tq: Match the specialised designation with the underlying ordinary court.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Courts - district designation, Special Public Prosecutor  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following qualifications is required for appointment as Special Public Prosecutor for a Human Rights Court?
o: A judicial officer who has completed ten years of service
An advocate who has practised for not less than three years
A public prosecutor or an advocate who has practised for not less than seven years
A retired police officer with seven years of service
accepted.x: For each Human Rights Court, the State Government specifies a Special Public Prosecutor who is a public prosecutor or an advocate in practice for not less than seven years.
accepted.tq: Test the exact minimum practice period and the permitted professional categories together.
accepted.sec: Human Rights Courts - district designation, Special Public Prosecutor  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about overlapping complaints before the NHRC and an SHRC:
1. An SHRC will not inquire into a case already being inquired into by the NHRC.
2. An SHRC will not inquire into a case already being inquired into by another statutory commission.
3. The NHRC does not take up a matter pending before an SHRC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The arrangement prevents simultaneous inquiry by the SHRC, NHRC or another statutory commission into the same pending matter.
accepted.tq: Check both directions of the non-overlapping jurisdiction rule before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: SHRC vs NHRC - overlapping complaints, transfer  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 2006 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act enabled the NHRC to:
o: Dissolve any SHRC without consultation
Convert every district court into a Human Rights Court
Transfer all NHRC members to State service
Transfer complaints to the concerned SHRC
accepted.x: The 2006 amendment enabled the NHRC to transfer complaints to the concerned State Human Rights Commission.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise transfer power and reject broader institutional powers not stated in the law.
accepted.sec: SHRC vs NHRC - overlapping complaints, transfer  [GROUP-II]
